extracted.intended_audience: readers of Popular Science Monthly; general educated public interested in natural science, public health, and technology
extracted.subtask_description: Identifying and applying criteria used in short popular-science reports to evaluate scientific claims, public-health recommendations, and technical apparatus descriptions. Covers judgement of reproducibility, evidential signs, experimental protocol, design requirements, and epidemiological/archaeological inference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific certainty (reproducibility)
rubrics_metrics.description: A fact is scientifically certain when the phenomenon, which is the evidence of it, can be reproduced at will by all persons who will use the same processes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as a standard for judging hypnotism and other psychological phenomena; reproducibility by independent observers using the same methods is the decisive test analogous to chemical or physical manipulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authenticity indicators for hypnotic/somnambulistic phenomena
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain recurring signs (closed eyelids, fibrillar movements in the facial muscles, hallucinations of vision and hearing, catalepsy, contracture) and the inability of subjects to simulate prolonged contractures or anatomically-specific reactions are indicators that hypnotic phenomena are real rather than simulation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Arguments include (1) implausibility of universal collusion to simulate, (2) long-standing agreement among reported phenomena over sixty years, (3) phenomena requiring anatomical/physiological knowledge unlikely to be feigned (e.g., specific muscle contractions on nerve pressure), (4) prolonged contractures without fatigue, (5) tolerance of painful tests without resistance. Variability between observers/subjects does not invalidate phenomena; focus on resemblances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experimental protocol for cold-exposure (refrigeration) studies
rubrics_metrics.description: Expose a healthy person to a water bath at 50° for durations from a quarter of a minute to five minutes, record body temperature during exposure and every five minutes in succeeding hours.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Observe that body temperature hardly varies during brief exposure but can fall after exertion or active reaction; drying/dressing and remaining still affects subsequent temperature; pulse changes (initial quickening, then slowing) should be recorded. Control for exertion because activity can cause sudden temperature fall and prolonged reduction persists for hours.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parameters and application rules for mechanical vibration therapy (percuteur use)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use an instrument (percuteur) giving a known number of blows per second applied over affected nerves; match vibration frequency to pain type—higher vibrations per second tend to relieve dull/aching/grinding pain, slower movements often arrest acute, quick pains.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply to nerves that can be thrown into mechanical vibration (superficial nerves give clearer effects); sensations progress from tingling to numbness to muscle twitching; deeper-seated nerves are more difficult to treat; theoretical basis: opposing pathological nervous vibrations by counter-vibrations. Devices (tuning-forks, modified apparatus) may produce local analgesia/anaesthesia; results reported as sometimes rapid and remarkable but not yet decisive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Geological inference criteria for past glaciation
rubrics_metrics.description: Use distribution of erratic boulders, glaciation of rocks in situ (especially in narrow gorges), presence or absence of moraines, and relative positions/elevations of similar rock bodies to infer former glacier extent and dynamics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider alternative transport mechanisms (force-torrents, creeping movement from undermining soil). Absence of moraines may indicate morainal ridges destroyed by later river erosion. Patterns such as concentration of granite boulders on one valley side, or stranded boulders on flood-planes, can suggest glaciers filled valleys to brim or transported boulders across valley widths. Use specific locality examples (Yellowstone Valley) and consider timing relative to valley erosion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sanitary ventilation standards for habitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Aim to secure for each habitable room (especially crowded cottages) a suitable provision for a constant change of air; ensure beds are not placed in close corners remote from door, window, and fireplace.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Derived from observations associating defective ventilation or polluted neighboring sources with pneumonia, lung disorders, tubercular meningitis, and convulsions in children. When transforming old houses, ensure fresh-air provision is not neglected or obstructed by partition arrangement. Specific defects observed include absence or closing of fireplaces/air exits and beds placed in close corners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design and operational criteria for continuous sewage filtration (Farquhar apparatus)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prevent formation of an impervious slimy deposit by providing continuous removal of the slime: enclose the filter-bed in a cylinder with a revolving cutter-plate that scrapes off the top deposit and forces it up an inclined plane; distribute incoming liquid via a hollow screw-spindle to the underside of the cutter-plate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operation produces a new clean surface continuously on the filter-bed; cutter-plate may revolve and be made to descend. Performance metrics from trial: with a 9.5-inch bed filtered 8 litres/min under 1.5 atm; scale-up projections for 1-foot and 10-foot diameters given (gallons/min and gallons/day). Use of pressure and bed diameter for capacity estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factors and investigative criteria for industrial explosions
rubrics_metrics.description: Analyze explosion statistics by material/machinery exposure and identify causes divided among bad design, workmanship, material, and ignorance/carelessness of attendants; recognize dust and novel chemical combinations as important hazards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use historical statistics (deaths per year by type: fire-damp, boilers, chemicals) and industry-specific patterns (e.g., saw/planing mills, steam-vessels, locomotives). Note seasonal/monthly patterns in colliery explosions and consider meteorological investigations. Recognize isolated storage locations' vulnerability to lightning. Investigate dust as an explosive agent in flour/processing mills and the interaction of chemicals (examples: nitrate of soda + sulphur reacting when water introduced).

rubrics_metrics.name: Determinants of extinction risk for large-bodied species
rubrics_metrics.description: Species larger than congeners are threatened due to (1) competition from humans, (2) being hunted with profit or destroyed for human security, (3) requiring more abundant food, and (4) having less frequent and more limited reproduction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these biological and anthropogenic factors to explain progressive diminution and extinction risk; list of vulnerable taxa provided as examples (whales, elephants, rhinoceroses, large carnivores, giraffes, bison, etc.). Smaller, highly fertile species maintain numbers despite human pressure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Epidemiological observations for diphtheria etiology
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider that diphtheria may be more common in rural than urban districts; it sometimes occurs concurrently with typhoid or scarlatina, suggesting possible common causative agents; distribution not consistently tied to damp soils and can appear on gravelly well-drained soils; seasonal patterns are not reliable though outbreaks often begin in October and occur in winter months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These observations contradict some prevailing views linking diphtheria to damp subsoils or houses shut in by trees. Use local case surveillance and soil/situational assessment; do not rely solely on meteorological data for predicting fluctuations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Archaeological and anthropological evidence criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Use collections of skulls, skeletons, prehistoric and modern relics, and artifacts (hatchets, arrow-heads, bronzes, potteries, fibulae) to infer population composition, cultural contacts, chronology (e.g., transition from bronze to iron), and possible colonization or trade connections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comparative morphology of artifacts (similar forms across distant regions) can indicate cultural transmission or colonists; craniology (large samples of skulls) and skeletons inform racial diversity and antiquity (stone-age remains). Use stratigraphic and typological context (e.g., neolithic implements, Etruscan potteries) and museum/exhibition records to support inferences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Taxonomic criteria for distinguishing phaeodaria from radiolaria
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize phaeodaria as a new group of marine siliceous rhizopods previously included among typical radiolaria but presenting considerable points of difference and rich in specific forms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Base distinction on morphological and distributional differences highlighted by deep-sea collections (e.g., findings of the Challenger Expedition); richness in specific forms and notable differences warrant separate taxonomic recognition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Environmental indicators linking poor air quality to specific diseases
rubrics_metrics.description: Associate impure air arising from defective ventilation or noxious surroundings (adjacent byres, pig-styes, stables, water-closets, sewers) with increased incidence of pneumonia, respiratory disorders following measles/whooping-cough, inflammatory affections of the brain, tubercular meningitis, and convulsions in children.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document observed defects such as closed air exits, lack of fireplace/vent, crowded beds in close corners, and proximity to filth sources. Use sanitary inspection of interior and surroundings to establish causal associations and implement airflow improvements and bed positioning as preventive measures.
